conversation.speaker: Student

conversation.speaker: Student

conversation.speaker: Librarian

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: Dr. Okafor, I got my lab report back, and I don't understand why I lost so many points on the discussion section.

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: Let's look at it together. Your results are accurate, but the discussion only repeats them. It doesn't explain what they mean.

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: I thought describing the results carefully was the point.

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: That belongs in the results section. The discussion should compare your findings with what the theory predicted, and explain any differences.

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: So I should have mentioned that our reaction was slower than expected?

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: Exactly, and suggested why. Perhaps the temperature wasn't constant. That kind of reasoning is what earns the points.

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: Can I rewrite it for a better grade?

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: You can resubmit the discussion section by next Friday, and I'll average the two grades.

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: Professor Lindqvist, I'd like to write my term paper on how social media affects elections, but I'm not sure the topic is suitable.

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: It's suitable, but far too broad. You could write five books on it. What part interests you most?

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: I'm curious whether political advertising online actually changes anyone's vote.

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: Better. Now narrow it to one country and one election, so you can work with real data.

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: Would the most recent national election here work? There was a lot of reporting on online ads.

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: It would. Be careful, though: news reports are not evidence of an effect. Look for academic studies that measured voting behavior.

conversation.speaker: Student
conversation.text: Where should I start looking?

conversation.speaker: Professor
conversation.text: Start with the two articles on the course reading list under week nine, and follow their references. Send me a one-page outline by the end of the month.
